item.research_question: Does the equiatomic AlAgCuNiSnTi alloy meet the criteria for a high entropy alloy, and what are its microstructural, thermal, and corrosion properties?
item.material_system: AlAgCuNiSnTi equiatomic multicomponent alloy (six elements in equal atomic concentrations)
item.processing_route: Vacuum Arc Remelting (VAR) using MRF-ABJ900 equipment under argon atmosphere; five remelting cycles; samples also processed via melt spinning to obtain ~1 mm thick strips; homogenization heat treatment at 800 °C
item.test_conditions: Microhardness measured with FM-700 AHOTEC tester (HV0.1/15); thermal analysis via DTA and DIL at 10 °C/min heating/cooling rates; corrosion testing in 3.5% NaCl solution using potentiodynamic method with BioLogic SP-150
key_findings: The alloy does not meet high entropy alloy criteria; ΔHmix = −10.13 kJ/mol and δ = 8.92 place it in the intermediate phase alloy range.
The as-cast microstructure is three-phase (four phases identified by XRD: TiNiSn, Ag3Sn, Al1.33Cu0.67, and Sn5Ti6).
Average microhardness of the as-cast alloy is 487 HV0.1/15, with the TiNi1.056Sn phase reaching a maximum of 600 HV0.1/15.
The corrosion rate stabilizes at 0.004 mm/y after initial passivation in 3.5% NaCl solution.
The corrosion rate (0.004 mm/y) is better than FeNiCoMnCrAl (0.009 mm/y) and FeNiCoMnCr (0.226 mm/y) HEAs in the same solution.
Homogenization at 800 °C did not cause major changes in the microstructure, though it slightly decreased hardness.
Melt spinning produced ~1 mm thick strips with a more homogeneous and grain-refined microstructure compared to the cast ingot.
item.mechanism: The authors argue that the alloy forms intermediate phases rather than a single solid solution due to thermodynamic parameters (ΔHmix and δ) falling outside the high entropy alloy range. The high corrosion resistance is attributed to the positive action of titanium oxide forming a passivation layer on the surface.
item.limitations: The alloy does not meet the criteria to be classified as a high entropy alloy; it contains multiple phases (intermetallics) rather than a single solid solution structure.
item.future_work: The authors propose that the alloy can be used for surface coating applications due to its high corrosion resistance.
quotes: The results show that the as-cast alloy microstructure is three-phase, with an average microhardness of 487 HV0.1/15.

The evolution of the corrosion resistance indicate an initially high corrosion rate, that decreases very quickly due to passivation of the alloy surface, and stabilizes at a value of 0.004 (mm/y (millimeters per year)).
Although the alloy examined contains six different alloying elements in equimolar concentrations, the calculations and microstructural aspects indicate there is no high entropy.
